details.description: Pakistan Meteorological Department Modernization of Hydromet Services of PMD in Pakistan (MHSP) Integrated Flood Resilience and Adaptation Project (IFRAP) INVITATION FOR PROPOSALS (NON-CONSULTING SERVICES – OPEN NATIONAL COMPETITION) Country Pakistan Name of Project Integrated Flood Resilience and Adaptation Project (IFRAP) (Component-2: Strengthening Hydromet and Climate Services) / Modernization of Hydromet Services of PMD in Pakistan (MHSP) Credit No. IDA-73330 Contract Title Establishment of Media Studios and Related Capacity Building RFP / STEP Reference No. PK-PMD-568943-NC-RFP The Islamic Republic of Pakistan has received financing from the International Development Association (IDA) towards the cost of the Integrated Flood Resilience and Adaptation Project (IFRAP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds to eligible payments under the contract for Establishment of Media Studios and Related Capacity Building. The Project Implementation Unit (PIU), Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) invites sealed Proposals from eligible Service Providers for the establishment of three (03) regional media studios at Peshawar, Lahore and Quetta, including studio fit-out, equipment supply and commissioning, capacity building of fifteen (15) PMD staff, pilot productions, documentaries and knowledge transfer. The duration of the assignment is twelve (12) months. The procurement will be conducted through open national competition using the Single-Stage Two-Envelope procedure with post-qualification and rated technical criteria, in accordance with the World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services (November 2020). The Contract will be awarded to the substantially responsive, qualified Service Provider obtaining the highest combined score (70% technical and 30% financial). The Request for Proposals (RFP), including the scope of work, equipment specifications, and qualification and evaluation criteria, and any addenda are available at https://weather.gov.pk/home/circulars#tender. Proposals, with the Technical Proposal and the Financial Proposal in separate sealed envelopes enclosed in one outer envelope, must be delivered to the address below by 1500 hours Pakistan Standard Time on 23 November 2026. Electronic submissions will not be accepted, and late Proposals will be rejected. Technical Proposals will be opened in public at 1530 hours on the same date, in the presence of the representatives

details.description: GOVERNMENT OF JAMAICA MINISTRY OF EDUCATION, SKILLS, YOUTH AND INFORMATION REQUEST FOR BIDS Country: Jamaica Name of Project: Jamaica Education Project (JEP) Loan No.: 9586-JM Assignment Title: Supply and Delivery of Audio-Visual Equipment for 183 Secondary Schools Reference No.: JM-MOEY-572540-GO-RFB The Government of Jamaica has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Jamaica Education Project (JEP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Government of Jamaica, through the Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth and Information (MoESYI) is seeking to address identified structural challenges in secondary education, through the Jamaica Education Project (JEP). The project is being implemented by the MoESYI with funding support provided by the World Bank, through a loan facility of US$30,000,000.00. It has five main components, : (i) Strengthening Teaching and Learning in Secondary Education; (ii) Supporting quality and resilient school infrastructure (iii) Strengthening information systems and strategies for student retention; (iv) Technical Assistance (TA), Strengthening Institutional Capacity and Project Management and (v) Contingent Emergency Response Component. A Project Implementation Unit has been established to accomplish the deliverables under each component of the Project. The Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth & Information (MoESYI) now invites eligible bidders to submit bids for the Supply and Delivery of Audio Visual Equipment for One Hundred and Eighty-Three (183) Secondary Schools . Details of the items to be procured (description, specifications and quantities), names and locations of the 183 schools are provided in Section VII of the bidding document. The procurement method/market approach is International Competitive Bidding (ICB) , utilizing the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Guidelines”), and is open to all eligible bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations. The attention of interested Bidders is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on Conflict of Interest. Availability of Documents The bidding document will be available for download as of October 20, 2026, on the Government of Jamaica Electronic Procurement website at www.gojep.gov.jm . details.description: Die Lernangebote beziehen sich auf die Förderung von Basiskompetenzen und die Unterstützung in der fachlichen Kompetenzentwicklung in den Schulformen der Ausbildungsvorbereitung, Berufsfachschule, Fachoberschule und der beruflichen Oberstufengymnasien. Darüber hinaus ist auch eine Förderung in den Bereichen BNE/Globales Lernen, Sprachbildung, Teambildung und Demokratiebildung möglich. Die Leistungserbringung findet während des Schuljahres statt. Als Förderangebote können sowohl integrative als auch unterrichtsergänzende Fördermaßnahmen, Zusatzangebote und Projekte entwickelt und umgesetzt werden. Die Fördermaßnahmen und die Angebotsschwerpunkte werden vom Rahmenvertragspartner in Abstimmung mit der Schule und ggf. den Subpartnern beim Ministerium für Bildung und Kultur beantragt. Eine enge Abstimmung der Schule mit dem Rahmenvertragspartner/Subpartner erfolgt auch in Fragen der Organisation und Durchführung. Das eingesetzte Personal für die Fördermaßnahmen und die Lehrkräfte der teilnehmenden Schülerinnen und Schüler stimmen sich zu den konkreten Inhalten, dem erforderlichen Lehr- und Lernmaterial und den Methoden ab. Bei der Auswahl der Maßnahmen ist auf eine Abgrenzung zum Aufgabengebiet der Schulsozialarbeit im Rahmen des Programms "Soziale Arbeit in den öffentlichen Berufsbildungszentren im Saarland" zu achten. Förderangebote können in Abhängigkeit der individuellen Konzeption integrativ, während der Schulzeit oder additiv, etwa im Nachmittagsbereich, stattfinden. Die Förderangebote finden als schulische Veranstaltung in der Verantwortung der jeweiligen Schule statt. Das integrative und additive Förderangebot wird vom Ministerium für Bildung und Kultur finanziert. Die Schulen entscheiden über die Räumlichkeiten, in denen das Angebot stattfindet. Der Rahmenvertragspartner stellt das für die Durchführung des Förderangebots erforderliche geeignete und qualifizierte Personal (beispielsweise auch pädagogische Fachkräfte, (Lehramt-)studierende, Lernpaten und Honorarkräfte) entweder selbst oder durch Kooperation mit anderen Partnern ("Subpartnern"). Subpartner können zum Beispiel Vereine, Verbände, Solo-künstlerinnen und Solokünstler sowie Anbieter kreativer Praxis sein. Bedient sich der Rahmenvertragspartner Subpartnern, so bleibt dennoch er Ansprechpartner und Vertragspartner des Ministeriums für Bildung und Kultur und ist diesem gegenüber für die ordnungsgemäße Leistungsausführung verantwortlich. details.description: Technological University Dublin (TU Dublin), has supported the delivery of Enterprise Ireland’s New Frontiers programme across the Dublin region since the programme launched nationally in 2012. The New Frontiers programme equips ambitious founders with the right connections, the right skills, and the right route to capital. It empowers them to take an idea or early-stage business through the initial development phases and prepare for their first phases of funding and growth. The programme is structured in three Phases of support and development. This procurement process aimed at recruiting a panel of business experts and facilitators to provide business focussed insights, practical workshops and advice to Phases 2 and 3 of the programme. Phase 2 is delivered full time over 6 months, involving workshops, one to one clinics and other supports. Following a separate competitive selection process, committed participants who have a strong value proposition and who can demonstrate that their business proposition has potential to grow and create jobs may be offered a place on Phase 2. Phase 3 Businesses emerging from Phase 2 will be guided to the most relevant government supports that can best help them at their particular stage of development. Further incubation facilities and support may be available to participants for a limited period, in conjunction with ongoing support from the Incubation Centre Management.
